title: Diagonals Separated Morphisms and Valuative Uniqueness

items.title: Locally closed immersions
items.statement: An immersion factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target. The condition is existence of such a factorization, not a chosen factorization.

items.title: Closed immersions: target locality and composition
items.statement: Closed immersion is local on an arbitrary open cover of the target, and closed immersions compose. An immersion with closed underlying image is a closed immersion.
items.strategy: Glue the local inverse homeomorphisms onto the closed image; stalkwise surjectivity is local. For composition use compositions of the surjective stalk maps and closed embeddings. For the final clause cover the target by the immersion factorization open and the complement of its now closed image.

items.title: Every scheme diagonal is an immersion
items.statement: For any X to S, Delta is an immersion. On compatible affine charts U=Spec B over W=Spec A its restriction over U times_W U is induced by multiplication B tensor_A B to B. Its point image consists of the canonical diagonal residue-field points, not all points whose two projections coincide.
items.strategy: Multiplication is onto. The union of U times_W U contains the diagonal image, though it need not cover the whole product. Glue the closed immersions into this union. At x the point is the prime kernel of kappa(x) tensor_kappa(s) kappa(x) to kappa(x).

items.title: Separated morphisms
items.statement: A morphism X to S is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion.

items.title: Relative and absolute separatedness
items.statement: An S-scheme is separated over S when its structure morphism is separated; absolute separatedness means over Spec Z.

items.title: Separatedness is local on the base
items.statement: X to S is separated iff its restrictions over an open cover of S are separated.
items.strategy: Pull back to base opens in one direction; the products over those opens cover X times_S X in the other.

items.title: Affine morphisms are separated
items.statement: Every affine morphism is separated.
items.strategy: On each affine base chart its source is affine; multiplication on the tensor algebra is surjective.

items.title: Affine schemes are separated
items.statement: Every map between affine schemes is separated; every affine scheme is separated over Spec Z.
items.strategy: A map between affines is affine by target-locality of affineness, using the one-chart cover.

items.title: Separatedness survives arbitrary base change
items.statement: Every base change of a separated morphism is separated.
items.strategy: Identify the new diagonal with the pullback of the old closed immersion. No flatness or finite-type condition.

items.title: The diagonal of a composite
items.statement: For X to Y to S the diagonal factors through X times_Y X; the map X times_Y X to X times_S X is the pullback of Delta_Y/S along (f,f).
items.strategy: Describe both fibre products on arbitrary test schemes and check both projections.

items.title: Separated morphisms compose
items.statement: A composite of separated morphisms is separated.
items.strategy: The factorization is a composite of two closed immersions.

items.title: Monomorphisms and diagonals
items.statement: A scheme morphism is a monomorphism iff its diagonal is an isomorphism. Monomorphism tests all schemes, including nonreduced ones. Consequently every monomorphism is separated.
items.strategy: If f is monic the two product projections are equal and either inverts Delta. Conversely compose any two test maps with their paired map into the product. Isomorphisms are closed immersions, proving the separation assertion.

items.title: Immersions are monomorphisms locally of finite type
items.statement: Every immersion is a monomorphism and locally of finite type; finite presentation is not asserted for arbitrary closed immersions.
items.strategy: Monicity is inherited from the two factors. On a target open in the factorization the quotient algebra needs no algebra generators, regardless of how many ideal generators it needs. The auxiliary monomorphism rules use test maps: composition preserves cancellation, and a pair of maps to a pullback is determined by its two projections. The stalk-surjection criterion reduces maps into an immersion to its subspace and surjective local structure maps.

items.title: Immersions are separated
items.statement: Open, closed, and locally closed immersions are separated.
items.strategy: Their diagonals are isomorphisms, hence closed immersions.

items.title: Closed graphs for separated targets
items.statement: If Y is separated over S, the graph of any S-morphism X to Y is a closed immersion.
items.strategy: Pull back the target diagonal; no condition on X is needed.

items.title: Scheme-theoretic equalizers
items.statement: For two S-morphisms a,b:X to Y, the equalizer is X times_(Y times_S Y) Y. It is an immersion, and is closed if Y/S is separated. It represents equality of morphisms on every test scheme.
items.strategy: The paired map (a,b) pulls back Delta. Verify the factorization universal property. Equality of point maps without equality of residue maps is insufficient.

items.title: Schematically dense opens
items.statement: An open j:U into X is schematically dense if O_X to j_*O_U is injective.

items.title: Density and reducedness
items.statement: A topologically dense open of a reduced scheme is schematically dense. A closed subscheme through which a schematically dense open factors is the whole scheme.
items.strategy: On an affine open a section vanishing on the dense open has vanishing locus the whole spectrum, hence lies in the nilradical and is zero. For the final claim the ideal sheaf injects into O_X and restricts to zero, so is zero.

items.title: Reduced-to-separated uniqueness
items.statement: Two S-morphisms from a reduced X to separated Y/S that agree on a dense open agree everywhere. More generally schematic density of the agreement open suffices without reducedness.
items.strategy: The closed equalizer contains the open schematically; its ideal vanishes.

items.title: The diagonal detects quasi-separatedness
items.statement: The existing affine-intersection definition of quasi-separated X to S is equivalent to quasi-compactness of its diagonal. Separated morphisms are quasi-separated. Quasi-separatedness is local on the base.
items.strategy: On product charts U times_W V the inverse image is U intersect V. To pass from affine charts to all quasi-compact opens use finite affine refinement; for separatedness each inverse image is a quotient spectrum. Base locality follows by restricting the diagonal to the products over a base open cover and using target locality of quasi-compactness.

items.title: Permanence and cancellation for separation properties
items.statement: Separated and quasi-separated morphisms are stable under base change, composition, and fibre products. If g composed with f is separated (respectively quasi-separated), then f is. If g composed with f is quasi-compact and g is quasi-separated, f is quasi-compact.
items.strategy: Quasi-compact maps compose by successive preimages of quasi-compact opens. Use the composite-diagonal factorization and base change for quasi-separated permanence; factor each product into two base changes. For separated cancellation, the image of Delta_f is the inverse image of the closed image of Delta_gf under X times_Y X into X times_Z X; immersion plus closed image applies. For quasi-separated cancellation use affine opens of Y mapping into affines of Z, then the intersection criterion locally on Y. For quasi-compact cancellation factor f as its graph and the base change of gf; the graph is the pullback of the quasi-compact Delta_g.

items.title: Graphs, sections, and absolute separation
items.statement: Every graph is an immersion and is quasi-compact if its target is quasi-separated over the base. A section of a separated (respectively quasi-separated) morphism is closed (respectively quasi-compact); every section is an immersion. If S is separated, X over S is separated iff X is absolutely separated; every map from an affine scheme is separated. The corresponding equivalence holds for quasi-separatedness when S is quasi-separated, and for quasi-compact separation properties when S has the corresponding property. Fibre products of schemes with any one of these properties over a base with that property have that property.
items.strategy: Pull back the target diagonal for graphs. A section is its graph after S times_S X=X. Apply composition and cancellation to X to S to Spec Z; in the quasi-compact clauses use quasi-compact cancellation as well. For fibre products apply base change and composition to a projection. For affine sources use their absolute separatedness and cancellation.

items.title: The affine overlap criterion
items.statement: For an affine cover W_i=Spec R_i of S and affine covers U_ij of its inverse images, X/S is separated iff every U_ij intersect U_ik is affine and Gamma(U_ij) tensor_R_i Gamma(U_ik) to Gamma(U_ij intersect U_ik) is surjective. In particular this identifies the previously defined affine-overlap separation condition with separatedness. In particular, if X/S and S are separated, any two affine opens of X have affine intersection.
items.strategy: The diagonal over a product chart is the overlap map, and the displayed homomorphism induces it. Affine intersections alone are insufficient. For the last clause apply the criterion over Spec Z after absolute-separatedness cancellation/composition.

items.title: Projective-space charts over any base
items.statement: The charts Spec A[u_0,...,u_n]/(u_i-1) glue along D(u_j) by v_l=u_l/u_j; these glue over affine opens of an arbitrary S and commute with restriction of the base.
items.strategy: Check the inverse transition u_l=v_l/v_i and on triple overlaps (u_l/u_j)/(u_k/u_j)=u_l/u_k. Base restrictions localize only coefficients, so transitions commute. Refine nonaffine base overlaps by affines before applying the published affine gluing theorem.

items.title: Relative projective space
items.statement: For n>=0, P^n_S is the scheme constructed by the preceding chart gluing. For n=0 it is S; over the empty base it is empty. Homogeneous coordinates are chart notation, not an assertion that all scheme-valued points are global tuples.

items.title: The projective-space diagonal
items.statement: For every scheme S and n>=0, the diagonal of P^n_S/S is the closed subscheme with equations x_i y_j-x_j y_i; hence projective space is separated.
items.strategy: On chart x_i=y_j=1 the equations give x_j y_i=1 and y_l=x_l y_i. The quotient is exactly the overlap ring A[x_l/x_i,(x_j/x_i)^(-1)]. The ideals agree on chart overlaps by units. Do not invoke the classical Segre theorem or a future Proj construction.

items.title: The doubled-origin scheme is not separated
items.statement: Glue two copies of A^1_k along D(t) by the identity. The result is not separated over k, although their intersection is affine.
items.strategy: The cross-chart overlap homomorphism k[t] tensor_k k[t] to k[t,t^-1] has image k[t], missing t^-1. This is an A-page result; do not depend on the published B-page example.

items.title: Valuative lifting diagrams
items.statement: For every valuation ring R with K=Frac R, and every commuting square Spec K to X over Spec R to S, uniqueness means at most one lift Spec R to X; existence means at least one. All rings, fields and diagrams are quantified.

items.title: Closed subschemes containing the generic point
items.statement: A closed subscheme of Spec R, R a domain, through which Spec Frac R factors is Spec R itself. Thus any map Spec R to Y whose generic restriction factors through a closed immersion Z into Y factors uniquely through Z.
items.strategy: The ideal I in R maps to zero in its fraction field, so I=0. Apply this to the pullback closed subscheme.

items.title: Separatedness gives valuative uniqueness
items.statement: Every separated morphism satisfies uniqueness for every valuation ring, without finite type or quasi-separatedness hypotheses. The same uniqueness works for any integral affine test scheme and its generic point.
items.strategy: The equalizer of the two lifts is closed and contains the generic point scheme-theoretically.

items.title: Domination of local subrings
items.statement: For local subrings A contained in B of a fixed field, B dominates A when the maximal ideal of B contracts to that of A.

items.title: Maximal dominating subrings satisfy the valuation condition
items.statement: Assuming Choice, a local subring B of a field K maximal for domination among all local subrings of K has fraction field K, is integrally closed in K, and for every nonzero x in K contains x or x^-1.
items.strategy: If t is outside Frac B, adjoining a transcendental t and localizing at (m,t), or adjoining an integral multiple of algebraic t and using lying over, contradicts maximality. Integral elements in K similarly give a dominating localization, so lie in B. If x is absent then m B[x]=B[x], otherwise localize at a maximal ideal over m. Write 1=sum a_i x^i with a_i in m: multiplying by x^-d makes x^-1 integral since 1-a_0 is a unit. No circular appeal to the already-defined valuation characterization.

items.title: Valuation domination with prescribed fraction field
items.statement: Assuming Choice, every local subring A of any field K is dominated by a valuation subring R of K with Frac R=K. K need not equal Frac A.
items.strategy: Apply Zorn to the set of local subrings of K dominating A. For a chain the union is local: nonunits form the union of the compatible maximal ideals; contraction is preserved. A maximal element is maximal under any further domination, so apply the preceding lemma.

items.title: Valuation rings realize specializations
items.statement: Assuming Choice, if y generizes z in S and K extends kappa(y), there is Spec R to S with R a valuation ring of K, generic point mapping to y by the prescribed embedding and closed point mapping to z.
items.strategy: Choose Spec A around z, with primes p subset q for y,z. The local domain A_q/pA_q embeds in kappa(y) and hence K. Dominate it in K and use the local-ring-point bijection. Keep the prescribed field extension, rather than replacing it without explanation.

items.title: Quasi-compact images stable under specialization are closed
items.statement: Assuming Choice, a quasi-compact scheme morphism whose image is stable under specialization has closed image.
items.strategy: Over Spec A take a finite affine cover Spec B_i of the inverse image. Set I=intersection ker(A to B_i); A/I embeds in finite product B_i. Each prime containing I contains a minimal prime p over I, obtained by applying the minimal-prime lemma in its localization. Localizing the injection at p leaves a nonzero product, hence some nonzero factor; a prime of that factor contracts to p by minimality. Thus every point of V(I) specializes a point in the image. Empty inverse images give I=A. This proof spells out the finite-product reduction rather than using a B-page example as a supplier.

items.title: Valuative existence makes a quasi-compact immersion closed
items.statement: Assuming Choice, a quasi-compact immersion j:Z to T satisfying existence for every valuation diagram is a closed immersion.

references.title: Conrad Theorem 2.1 converse, specialized to immersions

items.strategy: Given z in Z and a specialization of j(z), realize it with field K=kappa(z). Existence puts its special point in the image. The image is therefore specialization-stable, hence closed. This restricted lemma avoids assuming the later properness page.

items.title: Valuative criterion for separatedness
items.statement: Assuming Choice, a quasi-separated morphism X to S is separated iff all valuation diagrams have at most one lift. In particular this holds for quasi-separated finite-type morphisms; finite type is unnecessary for this all-valuation-ring version.
items.strategy: Uniqueness of lifts for f is existence for Delta_f: the lower map is a pair (a,b) agreeing generically, hence a=b, which supplies the lift. Delta is a quasi-compact immersion, so the preceding lemma makes it closed.

items.title: The Hausdorff analogy has limits
items.statement: The underlying topological space of a scheme fibre product need not be the topological product; separatedness is a diagonal condition in schemes, not Hausdorffness of the point space.

items.title: All valuation rings means all
items.statement: The criterion here quantifies over every valuation ring and every compatible field-valued point, including extensions of residue fields. No DVR-only replacement has been proved on this page.

references.title: Conrad Remark 2.2, distinguished from the all-valuation theorem

title: Diagonals Separated Morphisms and Valuative Uniqueness — Examples

items.title: The affine-line diagonal ideal
items.statement: Over any scheme S the diagonal of A^1_S is cut out by x-y.
items.strategy: On Spec A the multiplication map A[x,y] to A[t] has kernel (x-y), by polynomial substitution; glue over the base.

items.title: The projective-line diagonal
items.statement: The diagonal of P^1_S is cut out by x_0 y_1-x_1 y_0.
items.strategy: On same-index charts get the difference of affine coordinates; on mixed charts get uv-1. These four quotient rings agree with the four overlap charts.

items.title: Missing limit points in the doubled-origin diagonal
items.statement: The two cross-origin points lie in the closure of, but not in, the doubled-origin diagonal.
items.strategy: In a cross-chart A^2 the diagonal image is V(x-y) intersect D(x), whose closure is V(x-y); its origin is missing. Reverse the chart labels for the other missing point.

items.title: Two valuative extensions at the doubled origin
items.statement: The generic map Spec k(t) into the doubled-origin line extends in two ways from Spec k[t]_(t).
items.strategy: Prove k[t]_(t) is a DVR using its order-of-vanishing normal form. Map into each affine chart by the same ring map; generic restrictions coincide on D(t), while closed points land at distinct origins.

items.title: Equations for polynomial graphs
items.statement: The graph of a polynomial S-map A^m_S to A^n_S is cut out by y_i-f_i(x).
items.strategy: Substitution identifies the quotient with the source polynomial ring over each affine base chart; the equations glue.

items.title: A separated scheme with non-Hausdorff point space
items.statement: For any field k, A^1_k is separated but its scheme point space is not Hausdorff.
items.strategy: The generic point belongs to every nonempty open and is distinct from (t); they have no disjoint neighbourhoods. In particular this supplies the infinite-field example in the design.

items.title: Uniqueness without existence
items.statement: D(t) into Spec k[t] satisfies valuative uniqueness, but the generic map Spec k(t) to D(t) does not extend over Spec k[t]_(t) with its natural base map.
items.strategy: An extension would send invertible t in k[t,t^-1] to the nonunit t in the local ring; impossible.

items.title: DVR tests can miss nonseparatedness
items.statement: Candidate witness retained for source closure: let V be the union of k[t^(1/n!)] localized at (t^(1/n!)) inside the union of k(t^(1/n!)). Glue two copies of Spec V along their common generic point and map to Spec V. This morphism is nonseparated but satisfies uniqueness for every DVR diagram.

references.title: Conrad Remark 2.2 supports the warning only, not this candidate counterexample; source blocker B8-S2

items.strategy: Verify within this leaf: V is a valuation domain of value group Q with exactly primes 0,m; the generic point is D(t). Under any map V to a DVR, either a positive monomial maps to zero (then every positive monomial does and the map factors through k), or all monomials have value zero by arbitrary divisibility in Z (then it factors through Frac V). A nonzero element is monomial times a unit. Both fibres are disjoint unions of points, giving uniqueness. The two identity charts are distinct V-valued extensions of the common generic map. FATAL open source obligation: a primary full-text treatment of this precise DVR-insufficiency witness has not yet been read; do not approve this candidate by the formal inventory alone.

items.title: Reducedness cannot be dropped
items.statement: Two maps Spec k[x,e]/(e^2,xe) to A^1_k given by t maps to x and x+e agree on the dense open D(x), but differ.
items.strategy: After inverting x, e vanishes. The nilradical (e) gives reduced quotient k[x], so D(x) is dense. At the origin e remains nonzero, and the ring maps differ.

items.title: Equal point maps need not be equal scheme morphisms
items.statement: Identity and conjugation on Spec C are distinct R-morphisms with identical underlying point maps; their scheme equalizer is empty.
items.strategy: The equalizer ideal contains i-(-i)=2i, a unit, so its quotient ring is zero.
